observations.text: On first entry (EIBCALEN = 0) and on PF3 exit the program sets CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN itself; there is no check that the signed-on user is an administrator before list/update/delete is allowed.

Inferred: confirmation can be bypassed. PF10 is accepted when CA-DELETE-REQUESTED or CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED is set (580-581) and the selected row number is unchanged (666-678, 1042-1047). If the user was asked to confirm an update ('U') and changes the same row's select code to 'D' before pressing PF10, the EVALUATE branch at 810-815 deletes the row immediately without the 'Delete HIGHLIGHTED row ? Press F10 to confirm' prompt.

Inferred: the filter-changed check in 1210-EDIT-ARRAY is ineffective. 1200-EDIT-INPUTS performs 1210-EDIT-ARRAY before 1230-EDIT-DESC and 1220-EDIT-TYPECD (965-972), which are the only places that set FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES/NO and FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES/NO; INITIALIZE WS-MISC-STORAGE at task start (500-502) leaves the flags as spaces, so the condition at 991 is never true.

DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION-LEN is computed as FUNCTION LENGTH of the 50-byte field WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN, i.e. always 50, not the trimmed length; updated descriptions are therefore stored as 50-character VARCHAR values padded with trailing spaces.

The no-change check compares descriptions case-insensitively, so a case-only change is reported as 'No change detected with respect to database values.'; however it does not set INPUT-ERROR, so pressing PF10 still performs the UPDATE.
In 8000-READ-FORWARD a failed FETCH (WHEN OTHER) is labelled 'C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD close' in the DB2 message, and a failed look-ahead FETCH (1681-1691) does not set WS-DB2-ERROR, unlike the main fetch.
8100-READ-BACKWARDS performs 9500-OPEN-BACKWARD-CURSOR but does not test WS-DB2-ERROR before fetching, unlike 8000-READ-FORWARD (1612-1614).

8100-READ-BACKWARDS treats every non-zero SQLCODE, including +100 (fewer than 7 earlier rows, e.g. after deletes by other users), as a DB2 error ('Error on fetch Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD'), leaving the top rows of the page empty.
Inferred: WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM is PIC 9(1); ADD +1 on page 9 truncates to 0 (no ON SIZE ERROR), after which 8000-READ-FORWARD resets it to 1 and the screen reports the first page.

CA-DELETE-SUCCEEDED and CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED share the value LOW-VALUES with CA-DELETE-NOT-REQUESTED / CA-UPDATE-NOT-REQUESTED, so 'succeeded' and 'not requested' are indistinguishable; INITIALIZE of the commarea sets the flags to spaces, matching none of the 88-levels.
PF2 (add) sets CDEMO-USRTYP-USER (not admin) and the message WS-EXIT-MESSAGE ('PF03 pressed. Exiting') before XCTL to COTRTUPC.

Inferred: WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03 in the main EVALUATE is unreachable in normal flow because PF3 already XCTLs away at 591-625. The WHEN at 721-722 duplicates the condition at 726-727 and has no statements of its own.

Working-storage items never referenced in the procedure division: WS-TYPE-CD-DELETE-FILTER (an SQL IN-list builder), TRAN-TYPE-CD-X/N, LIT-TRANTYPE-TABLE, FLG-ROW-DESCR-CHANGED-*, WS-ROW-SELECT-ERROR.
RESP of EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP and SEND MAP is captured in WS-RESP-CD but never tested.
Delete failures other than -532 (including +100 row not found) only format a message; INPUT-ERROR is not set and CA-DELETE-REQUESTED is not explicitly re-armed in that branch.
Page size WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES = 7 and schema CARDDEMO in all SQL statements are hard-coded.

paragraphs.logic: Initialises work areas, restores CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA (or initialises them on first entry), maps the AID key and, when re-entered from itself, receives and edits the screen. Handles PF3 (XCTL back to caller or COADM01C) and PF2 (XCTL to COTRTUPC), demotes invalid keys and unconfirmed PF10 to ENTER, checks DB2 connectivity, then EVALUATEs input error, PF7/PF8 paging, ENTER/PF10 for delete or update, or default refresh, and finally goes to COMMON-RETURN.

A non-numeric value sets INPUT-ERROR, FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK, protects the rows and sets 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER'. A numeric value becomes WS-TYPE-CD-FILTER with FLG-TYPEFILTER-ISVALID.

After the 7th row a look-ahead fetch sets CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS and WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE, or CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS. +100 ends the page ('No records found for this search condition.' when page 1 is empty); other SQLCODEs set WS-DB2-ERROR with a formatted message. Closes the cursor.

Any non-zero SQLCODE sets WS-DB2-ERROR with 'Error on fetch Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD'.

rules.outcome: EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) with CARDDEMO-COMMAREA.
rules.statement: PF3 returns to the calling transaction/program recorded in the commarea; if none is recorded (low-values, spaces or this program itself) it returns to the admin menu CA00 / COADM01C. A CICS SYNCPOINT is taken before the XCTL.

rules.conditions: CCARD-AID-PFK10 AND (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED OR CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED) AND FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-NO AND FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-NO AND FLG-ROW-SELECTION-CHANGED-NO
rules.outcome: Otherwise SET CCARD-AID-ENTER TO TRUE.
rules.statement: PF10 (confirm) is honoured only when a delete or update confirmation is pending and neither filter nor the selected row number has changed since the confirmation prompt; otherwise PF10 is processed as ENTER (re-validate and re-prompt). PF10 without a pending request is an invalid key and is also treated as ENTER.

messages: Db2 access failure.
rules.outcome: SEND TEXT WS-LONG-MSG and EXEC CICS RETURN (no TRANSID).
rules.statement: Before any list processing the program verifies DB2 connectivity with a priming query; if it fails, the formatted DB2 error is sent as plain text and the conversation ends.

rules.outcome: WS-RETURN-MSG to CCARD-ERROR-MSG; optional 8000-READ-FORWARD; 2000-SEND-MAP; COMMON-RETURN.
rules.statement: When any input edit fails, the screen is redisplayed with the error message; the current page is re-read from its first key only if neither filter is in error, so rows are not shown for an invalid or non-matching filter.

rules.outcome: 8000-READ-FORWARD or 8100-READ-BACKWARDS, INITIALIZE WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS, 2000-SEND-MAP.
rules.statement: Paging: PF8 moves to the next page only when CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS, starting at WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE (the first row of the next page) and incrementing the page number; PF7 on page 1 re-reads the first page ('No previous pages to display'); PF7 on later pages decrements the page number and reads backwards from WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE. Row selections are cleared when paging.

messages: Delete HIGHLIGHTED row ? Press F10 to confirm
rules.outcome: ENTER: prompt 'Delete HIGHLIGHTED row ? Press F10 to confirm'. PF10: 9300-DELETE-RECORD; on success FLG-DELETED-YES, send map, then INITIALIZE commarea and set first page.
rules.statement: Deleting a transaction type is a two-step action: ENTER with a 'D' selection redisplays the page and asks for confirmation; PF10 with the 'D' selection performs the DELETE. After a successful delete the screen shows the result and the list state is reset so the next interaction starts from the first page.

messages: Update HIGHLIGHTED row. Press F10 to save
rules.outcome: ENTER: prompt 'Update HIGHLIGHTED row. Press F10 to save'. PF10: 9200-UPDATE-RECORD; on success FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED; 8000-READ-FORWARD; 2000-SEND-MAP.
rules.statement: Updating a transaction type description is a two-step action: ENTER with a 'U' selection validates the new description and asks for confirmation; PF10 performs the UPDATE and then re-reads and redisplays the current page.

rules.outcome: WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN(I) = LOW-VALUES, else FUNCTION TRIM(TRTYPDI(I)).
rules.statement: A row description entered as '*' or all spaces is treated as not supplied (LOW-VALUES); any other entry is trimmed of leading and trailing spaces before validation and update.

messages: Action code selected is invalid
rules.outcome: INPUT-ERROR, WS-ROW-TRTSELECT-ERROR(I) = '1', FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-YES.
rules.statement: The only valid row action codes are 'D' (delete) and 'U' (update); blank means no action. Any other code marks the row in error and rejects the input with 'Action code selected is invalid'. A 'U' row triggers the description edit.

messages: Please select only 1 action
rules.outcome: INPUT-ERROR with message 'Please select only 1 action'.
rules.statement: Only one row action may be requested per screen: if more than one select field is non-blank, the input is rejected with 'Please select only 1 action' and the selected rows are flagged in error.

rules.outcome: WS-EDIT-SELECT-FLAGS initialised; exit 1210-EDIT-ARRAY.
rules.statement: Intended rule: if either filter was changed, all row selections are discarded and no row action is processed. As coded the change flags are evaluated before the filter edits set them, so this reset does not take effect (see observation).

rules.conditions: UPPER(TRIM(WS-ROW-TR-DESC-IN(I))) = UPPER(TRIM(WS-CA-ROW-TR-DESC-OUT(I))) and equal trimmed lengths
messages: No change detected with respect to database values.
rules.outcome: WS-RETURN-MSG = 'No change detected with respect to database values.'; INPUT-ERROR is not set.
rules.statement: An update whose new description equals the current database description, ignoring case and leading/trailing spaces, is reported as 'No change detected with respect to database values.' and the description is not re-validated.

rules.anchor: ' can have numbers or alphabets only.'
rules.conditions: Description empty, or contains a character outside LIT-UPPER, LIT-LOWER, LIT-NUMBERS and space
messages: must be supplied.
can have numbers or alphabets only.
rules.outcome: INPUT-ERROR; FLG-ALPHNANUM-BLANK or FLG-ALPHNANUM-NOT-OK; message only if no earlier message.
rules.statement: A changed transaction type description is mandatory and may contain only letters (A-Z, a-z), digits and spaces; otherwise the input is rejected with 'Transaction Desc must be supplied.' or 'Transaction Desc can have numbers or alphabets only.' and the description is highlighted.

rules.conditions: WS-IN-TYPE-CD not LOW-VALUES/SPACES/ZEROS and NOT NUMERIC
messages: TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER
rules.outcome: INPUT-ERROR, FLG-TYPEFILTER-NOT-OK, FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES; else WS-TYPE-CD-FILTER = WS-IN-TYPE-CD with FLG-TYPEFILTER-ISVALID.
rules.statement: The transaction type code filter is optional (blank, spaces or '00' mean no filter); if supplied it must be numeric (2 digits), otherwise the input is rejected with 'TYPE CODE FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 2 DIGIT NUMBER' and row selection is disabled.

rules.conditions: WS-IN-TYPE-CD <> WS-CA-TYPE-CD (unless both empty); WS-IN-TYPE-DESC <> WS-CA-TYPE-DESC (unless both empty)
rules.outcome: INITIALIZE WS-CA-PAGING-VARIABLES; FLG-TYPEFILTER-CHANGED-YES / FLG-DESCFILTER-CHANGED-YES.
rules.statement: Changing either search filter (type code or description) restarts paging: the saved paging state (first/last keys, page number, next-page indicator) is cleared and the new filter value is remembered in the commarea.

rules.outcome: FLG-DESCFILTER-ISVALID; WS-TYPE-DESC-FILTER = '%' || TRIM(input) || '%'.
rules.statement: A non-blank description filter is applied as a 'contains' search: TR_DESCRIPTION LIKE '%<trimmed filter>%'. Inferred: the match is case-sensitive because the column is compared as stored without case folding.

rules.anchor: 'No Records found for these filter conditions'
messages: No Records found for these filter conditions
Error reading TRANSACTION_TYPE table
rules.outcome: INPUT-ERROR, filter flags NOT-OK, FLG-PROTECT-SELECT-ROWS-YES.
rules.statement: When a type or description filter is supplied, the program counts matching TRANSACTION_TYPE rows first; if none match, the input is rejected with 'No Records found for these filter conditions', the supplied filters are flagged in error and row selection is disabled. A SQL error on the count is also treated as an input error with a formatted DB2 message.

rules.conditions: C-TR-TYPE-FORWARD: TR_TYPE >= WS-START-KEY, optional TR_TYPE = filter, optional TR_DESCRIPTION LIKE filter, ORDER BY TR_TYPE
messages: No records found for this search condition.
No more pages for these search conditions
rules.outcome: WS-CA-ROW-*-OUT(1..7), WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE, WS-CA-LAST-TR-CODE, CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS/NOT-EXISTS.
rules.statement: The list shows at most 7 transaction types per page in ascending TR_TYPE order starting at the page start key and honouring the active filters. An eighth row is fetched only to decide whether a next page exists and to set the next page's start key. If page 1 has no rows the message 'No records found for this search condition.' is shown; pressing PF8 at the end shows 'No more pages for these search conditions'. Other SQL errors stop the read with a formatted DB2 message.

rules.conditions: C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD: TR_TYPE < WS-START-KEY with the same filters, ORDER BY TR_TYPE DESC
messages: Error on fetch Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD
rules.outcome: Rows filled from 7 to 1; WS-CA-FIRST-TR-CODE updated; on error WS-DB2-ERROR with 'Error on fetch Cursor C-TR-TYPE-BACKWARD'.
rules.statement: Page back reads the 7 transaction types immediately before the current page's first code (TR_TYPE < start key, descending) and places them in rows 7 down to 1, so the page is shown in ascending order; the new first code becomes the start key. Any fetch that does not return a row is treated as a DB2 error.

rules.conditions: DELETE-REQUESTED-ON(I) / UPDATE-REQUESTED-ON(I) AND WS-ONLY-1-VALID-ACTION AND FLG-BAD-ACTIONS-SELECTED-NO
rules.outcome: CA-DELETE-REQUESTED / CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED set, or SELECT-BLANK(I) when FLG-DELETED-YES / FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED.
rules.statement: A confirmation is armed (CA-DELETE-REQUESTED or CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED stored in the commarea) only when exactly one valid action is selected and no row has an invalid action; after a completed delete or update the row's select code is cleared.

rules.conditions: FLG-DELETED-YES, FLG-UPDATE-COMPLETED, filter flags, AID key, CA-FIRST-PAGE, CA-NEXT-PAGE-NOT-EXISTS, CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN
messages: HIGHLIGHTED row deleted.Hit Enter to continue
HIGHLIGHTED row was updated
No previous pages to display
No more pages to display
Type U to update, D to delete any record
rules.outcome: WS-INFO-MSG / WS-RETURN-MSG set; CA-LAST-PAGE-SHOWN set on first PF8 at the end.
rules.statement: Screen messages follow a fixed priority: delete success, update success, filter errors (no info message), confirmation prompts for a single delete/update on ENTER (only if filters unchanged), 'No previous pages to display' on PF7 at page 1, 'No more pages to display' on PF8 once the last page has already been shown, otherwise the hint 'Type U to update, D to delete any record'.

rules.conditions: UPDATE CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE SET TR_DESCRIPTION = :DCL-TR-DESCRIPTION WHERE TR_TYPE = :DCL-TR-TYPE
messages: Record not found. Deleted by others ?
Deadlock. Someone else updating ?
Update failed with
rules.outcome: 0: SYNCPOINT, CA-UPDATE-SUCCEEDED, 'HIGHLIGHTED row was updated'; else CA-UPDATE-REQUESTED and formatted DB2 message.
rules.statement: A confirmed description update is committed (CICS SYNCPOINT) only on SQLCODE 0. Row not found (+100, 'Record not found. Deleted by others ? '), deadlock/timeout (-911, 'Deadlock. Someone else updating ?', also an input error) and other negative SQLCODEs ('Update failed with') keep the update request pending so the user can retry.

messages: Please delete associated child records first:
Delete failed with message:
rules.outcome: 0: SYNCPOINT, CA-DELETE-SUCCEEDED, 'HIGHLIGHTED row deleted.Hit Enter to continue'; -532: CA-DELETE-REQUESTED + message; other: message.
rules.statement: A transaction type that still has category rows cannot be deleted: SQLCODE -532 (delete restricted by the TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY foreign key ON DELETE RESTRICT) produces 'Please delete associated child records first:' and keeps the delete pending. A successful delete is committed with CICS SYNCPOINT; any other SQLCODE produces 'Delete failed with message:'.

sme_questions.question: Should PF10 be refused when the pending confirmation type (update) differs from the action now selected on the same row (delete)? As coded a 'U' prompt followed by changing the code to 'D' and pressing PF10 deletes without a delete prompt.
Is a case-only description change meant to be blocked? The program reports 'No change detected' but still performs the UPDATE on PF10.
Should the stored TR_DESCRIPTION length be the trimmed length rather than always 50?
Which users may run CTLI? The program sets CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN itself without checking the signed-on user type; is access control enforced elsewhere (menu COADM01C, CICS security)?
Should filter changes clear pending row selections (the reset at 991-994 never fires because the change flags are set later in 1200-EDIT-INPUTS)?

summary.text: COTRTLIC is a pseudo-conversational CICS/DB2 program (transaction CTLI, map CTRTLIA in mapset COTRTLI) that lists rows of CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE, 7 per page, with optional filters on the 2-digit type code and on a description substring. Paging uses two DB2 cursors: a forward cursor (TR_TYPE >= start key, ascending, with an 8th-row look-ahead to detect a next page) for ENTER/PF8 and a backward cursor (TR_TYPE < first key, descending) for PF7. The user can mark one row with 'U' to edit its description or 'D' to delete it; ENTER validates and asks for confirmation and PF10 performs the UPDATE or DELETE, committing with CICS SYNCPOINT and handling not-found, deadlock (-911) and child-row restriction (-532) SQLCODEs. PF2 transfers to COTRTUPC (add/maintain screen) and PF3 returns to the caller or the admin menu COADM01C. A DB2 priming query checks connectivity first; state (filters, paging keys, displayed rows, pending action) is kept in the commarea appended to CARDDEMO-COMMAREA.
